entry_point: HTTP API: PUT/GET/DELETE /1.0/client/remotes[/{name}], PUT /1.0/client/remotes/{name}/refresh, DELETE /1.0/client/remotes (bulk), POST /1.0/ops/replication/rbd/{pool}; shared ceph config/keyring writers and database removal helper

verified.entry_point: At the pinned commit the import route writes a traversal-named remote conf/keyring outside ConfPath through the real handler; the removal, re-render, bulk-removal and replication-enable routes each reach their protected sink through the real handler with a traversal or reserved name, before any fix. All were reproduced offline by calling the registered handler functions with the real request plumbing and a temp snap-style state directory.

routes: Import (PUT /1.0/client/remotes/{name}): traversal in the body name writes conf/keyring outside the configuration area; reserved names overwrite the local cluster's ceph.conf/ceph.keyring/radosgw.conf; a body name different from the path name writes a different remote; an injected local name reaches the generated keyring; an over-long name is accepted.
Single removal (DELETE /1.0/client/remotes/{name}): a traversal name deletes a conf/keyring pair outside the configuration area; a reserved name deletes the local cluster's own files.
Re-render (PUT /1.0/client/remotes/{name}/refresh, injected): a traversal path name writes conf/keyring outside the configuration area through the shared writer.
Bulk removal (DELETE /1.0/client/remotes, injected): a traversal name in the body deletes a conf/keyring pair outside the configuration area through the database helper.

Replication enable (POST /1.0/ops/replication/rbd/{pool}): a remote name recorded by an earlier request is read from the database and written into the mirror peer token file name, escaping the mirror directory.
List and fetch (GET): the empty collection lookup lists all remotes; a single valid name fetches one. No file sink, so these are functional only.
injected_siblings: microceph/api/remote_refresh.go:35 cmdRemoteRefresh (PUT /1.0/client/remotes/{name}/refresh) re-renders an existing remote through renderConfAndKeyringFiles/WriteConfig without validating the path name; a maintainer adding credential rotation would naturally reuse the import renderer.

microceph/api/remote_refresh.go:60 cmdRemoteBulkDelete (DELETE /1.0/client/remotes with a body name list) removes several remotes through database.DeleteRemoteDb without validating each body name; a maintainer adding maintenance tooling would naturally reuse the single-remove helper.

wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the defect has no roles or directions; one name reaches every protected file, so there is no direction to fix separately.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every protected outcome is a file write or a file removal; the lookup route has no file effect, so a read-only guard cannot pass the write and removal checks.
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no normalising, clamping or unit-conversion step sits between the supplied name and the file path.
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: names are compared as opaque strings and no second decoding step sits between the validation point and the file operation, so a malformed spelling cannot make a checked name differ from the used name.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no role, secret or external authority lookup decides these requests.

traps.shape: producer off the check's path: a remote name recorded by an earlier request is read back from the database by the replication flow and becomes the mirror peer token file name; validating the import handler never sees it.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the replication enable flow reads the stored remote record and passes its name to the token writer, which trusted a value it had not seen arrive.

traps.shape: lower-level shared writer plus an additional remote route: the re-render route hands its path name to the same configuration/keyring writer the import flow uses.
traps.realistic_because: the route is the kind of credential-rotation helper a maintainer adds next to import, and it reuses the existing renderer; the shared writer also accepts the product's ordinary dotted file names, so a fix must not reject those.

traps.shape: database helper plus an additional removal route: bulk removal passes body-supplied names to the helper that removes the remote's conf/keyring files.
traps.realistic_because: bulk maintenance removal naturally reuses the single-remove database helper, and the reported import flow gives no reason to inspect it.

traps.shape: shape trap: a name that passes the character rules exactly matches the base name of a file the local cluster keeps, so a containment-or-alphabet check accepts it and the write or removal destroys the local cluster's own file.
traps.where: microceph/api/remote.go:47 and microceph/api/remote.go:105 (via the shared validator)
traps.realistic_because: the collision names are ordinary valid cluster names, and the product itself writes files under exactly those base names; the legitimate near-miss names must keep working.

traps.shape: wrong object: the request path identifies one remote while the body identifies another, and the old handler writes the body name without comparing them.
traps.realistic_because: the body name is the one the rendering code uses, so checking only it looks complete; the path is what a routing or authorising layer sees.

traps.shape: shape trap: the existing character regex accepts any length, so a plausible validator copied from it still accepts an over-long name.
traps.realistic_because: the product already had this exact regex in place for cluster export, which makes copying it the natural fix; the 63-character bound is stated in the report and the 63-character case must keep working.
